evals.prompt: We're Tallyfold, a meeting-notes SaaS (about 40 people, ~$6M ARR), everything runs on AWS in us-east-1. We just finished a Teams bot + meeting extension and our CRO wants to 'get on AppSource and get Microsoft reps selling us through co-sell', ideally so enterprise customers can burn their Azure commit on us. Plan: submit the Teams app this month, then apply for co-sell. Can you sanity-check the plan and tell me the steps?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the Teams app alone cannot reach co-sell status, that co-sell and MACC run on a transactable SaaS offer, that an AWS-hosted SaaS can transact but cannot become Azure IP co-sell eligible or draw down MACC, and gives a corrected path with the Teams app linked to a per-user transactable SaaS offer.
expectations: States that Teams apps (apps and add-ins for Microsoft 365/Office) are not eligible for co-sell-ready status
Recommends publishing a separate transactable SaaS offer (Sell through Microsoft) to carry co-sell
States that MACC drawdown requires Azure IP co-sell eligible status
States that Azure IP co-sell eligibility requires the SaaS to be primarily platformed on Azure, so the AWS-hosted product does not qualify
Tells the user that the 'burn Azure commit' goal is unavailable unless the product moves to Azure, rather than deferring it as a later step
Says a non-Azure SaaS can still list and transact only if it integrates with or extends a Microsoft product, and that the Teams app satisfies this
Recommends linking the Teams app to the SaaS offer through the manifest subscriptionOffer field
States that a Teams-linked SaaS offer must use per-user pricing
Mentions the $100,000 revenue threshold (Azure consumed revenue or marketplace billed) for IP co-sell eligibility
Describes co-sell ready as visibility to Microsoft sellers, not a source of referrals by itself
Mentions Publisher Verification as a prerequisite before the Teams submission
Mentions that Publisher Attestation is completed once the app is live in the store
Asks or states an assumption about who owns outreach to Microsoft sellers or the target date

evals.prompt: quick one: we're putting our API monitoring product (Pingwell) on Microsoft Marketplace. Plan is a Contact Me listing now so we're 'in the catalog', then in Q2 flip it to transactable with a flat monthly plan, and later add per-seat plans for bigger teams plus a usage meter for API calls. We also want the Teams app to sell the same offer. We'll test the checkout on the live offer with our own corporate card. Anything wrong with that?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the pricing model is fixed per offer at publish, that per-seat plans cannot be added to a flat-rate offer, that metering exists only on flat-rate plans while Teams-linked offers must be per user, that the listing-only to transact switch is uncertain across Microsoft pages, and that test purchases are invoiced so testing belongs on a separate offer or private plan.
expectations: States that all plans in one SaaS offer share one pricing model (flat rate or per user)
States that the pricing model cannot be changed after the offer is published
Says adding per-seat plans later to a flat-rate offer requires a new offer
States that metered billing is only available on flat-rate plans, not per-user plans
States that a SaaS offer linked to a Teams app must use per-user pricing
Concludes that one offer cannot serve both the Teams link and API-call metering, and proposes a resolution (separate offers or a model choice)
Flags uncertainty about switching a published Contact Me SaaS offer to transactable, and recommends building transact from the start or confirming with Microsoft support
Says a Contact Me listing unlocks no MACC, co-sell eligibility or private offers
Warns that test purchases on a live offer are actually invoiced
Recommends a separate test offer or a private plan at a nominal price for testing
Lists plan ID or metered dimension IDs among choices that lock at publish

evals.prompt: Our Teams app (Shiftlane, a rota and shift-swap app) got its second 'Attention needed' validation report. Issues: app name in Partner Center is 'Shiftlane for Teams' but manifest says 'Shiftlane', our validDomains include staging.shiftlane.io, and they said the bot 'does not respond to Help'. Also Partner Center keeps nagging about Publisher Attestation but the attestation form won't let us complete it. Marketing promised a launch date in 10 days. What do we fix, in what order, and is 10 days realistic? Our app name for the listing is just 'Shifts' in some places, by the way.
evals.expected_output: Gives a fix list (matching names across manifest and Partner Center, removing staging domains, bot handling Help/Hi with no dead ends, prefixing the common-noun name), explains attestation cannot be completed until a new app is live and should be done the day it lists, keeps Publisher Verification as a must-fix, explains the concierge reply and confirmation loop, and resets the 10-day expectation against Microsoft's multi-week sizing.
expectations: Requires the app name to match exactly across the manifest and Partner Center
Requires removing staging or non-production domains from validDomains
Requires the bot to respond to Help (and greetings) without dead ends
Flags 'Shifts' as a common noun that must be prefixed or suffixed with the publisher brand
Explains that a new app cannot complete Publisher Attestation until it is live in the Teams store
Recommends completing Publisher Attestation immediately after the app goes live and renewing it yearly
Mentions Publisher Verification as a Must fix item
Mentions the validation report categories (Must fix, Good-to-fix, Blocker, Query) or that only must-fix and blocker items gate approval
Tells the user to reply to the concierge email thread and wait for confirmation before resubmitting
Says the 10-day date is at risk and cites a multi-week planning range rather than the 24-hour report figure
Advises against changing app functionality during validation
Mentions that each resubmission needs a new manifest version number with the same app ID

evals.prompt: VP Sales here at Corvane (data-quality SaaS, hosted on Azure, ~$180k billed through Microsoft Marketplace so far, mostly two enterprise deals). We got 'Co-sell ready' in July. It's late October and we've had zero referrals from Microsoft. My CEO thinks Marketplace was a waste and wants to pull the listing. What do I tell him, and what should we actually be doing?
evals.expected_output: Explains co-sell ready is catalog visibility, checks the path to Azure IP co-sell eligible (already past the $100K billed threshold, needs Azure technical validation and reference architecture diagram), recommends partner-led co-sell with self-registered opportunities, account mapping to Microsoft sellers and a MACC drawdown pitch, private offers and renewal migration, and argues against pulling the listing.
expectations: Explains that co-sell ready status only makes the solution visible to Microsoft sellers and does not generate referrals by itself
Notes the company already exceeds the $100,000 marketplace billed revenue threshold for Azure IP co-sell eligible
Lists the reference architecture diagram as a remaining requirement for SaaS IP co-sell eligibility
Lists the Azure technical validation (primarily platformed on Azure) as a requirement
Explains that IP co-sell eligibility makes the offer count toward customers' MACC
Recommends registering their own opportunities in Partner Center rather than waiting for inbound referrals
Recommends mapping target accounts to Microsoft account executives and pitching MACC drawdown
Recommends using private offers for enterprise deals
Recommends moving existing customer renewals onto Marketplace private offers with the renewal self-attestation for the fee discount
Mentions Frontier Accelerate for Marketplace enrollment as a prerequisite or current home of co-sell benefits
Advises against pulling the listing, with a reason tied to MACC or private-offer procurement
Sets an expectation of months, not weeks, for seller engagement
Marks Microsoft thresholds or fees as needing verification in Partner Center

evals.prompt: Finance question. We sell Ledgerkite (AP automation, Azure-hosted, IP co-sell eligible). 1) A big customer's renewal is coming in January; their contract is off-marketplace today. 2) Another customer bought via a private offer we created in August 2024 that auto-renews next month. 3) A reseller in Germany wants to resell us to its customers through CSP and the customer wants it to count against their Azure commitment. What fee do we pay in each case and what should we set up?
evals.expected_output: Case 1: create a new private offer and self-attest it as a renewal for the 50% fee discount (1.5% instead of 3%) for the term. Case 2: offers created before October 1, 2024 are ineligible; the customer must cancel or stop auto-renew and accept a new attested private offer. Case 3: CSP private offers complete outside Marketplace and do not decrement MACC; use a multiparty private offer with the reseller if MACC drawdown matters.
expectations: States the standard store service fee is 3%
States the renewal discount halves the fee for customer private offer or multiparty private offer renewals
Says the renewal status must be self-attested during private offer creation
Recommends converting case 1 into a new private offer flagged as a renewal
States that private offers created before October 1, 2024 are not eligible for the renewal discount
Says case 2 needs auto-renew turned off or the subscription cancelled and a new attested private offer accepted
States that CSP private offers do not count toward the customer's MACC
Recommends a multiparty private offer with the German reseller when MACC drawdown is required
States a multiparty private offer allows only one channel partner
Marks fee figures as needing verification in Partner Center
States the renewal attestation must be made at private offer creation and cannot be added afterwards

evals.prompt: I'm the partnerships lead at Brightmoor (contract analytics SaaS on Azure, not yet on Marketplace). From some 2024 notes: step 1 apply to ISV Success for Azure credits, step 2 sign up for Marketplace Rewards, step 3 send our leads through the Qualified Referral Program, step 4 list on AppSource. Can you turn that into a current plan for the next quarter? We want our first Marketplace transaction by end of January.
evals.expected_output: Updates the stale plan: AppSource and Azure Marketplace are now Microsoft Marketplace, ISV Success and Marketplace Rewards were folded into Frontier Accelerate for Marketplace (no-cost and paid Premium tiers, enrollment a prerequisite for co-sell listing), QRP is retired and referrals live in Partner Center, and reorders around a transactable SaaS offer with a private offer as the first transaction, with figures flagged for verification.
expectations: States that AppSource and Azure Marketplace are now unified as Microsoft Marketplace
States that ISV Success and Marketplace Rewards were consolidated into Frontier Accelerate for Marketplace
Mentions that Frontier Accelerate has a no-cost tier and a paid Premium tier
States that Frontier Accelerate enrollment is a prerequisite for a co-sell listing
States that the Qualified Referral Program is retired and referrals are managed in Partner Center referrals
Puts a transactable SaaS offer (landing page, Fulfillment API, webhook, Entra SSO) on the critical path
Recommends the first transaction be a private offer
Mentions the tax profile and payout profile must be set up before transacting
Builds the timeline backward from the end-of-January target
Includes at least one failed certification cycle in the timeline
Flags program names, prices or criteria as needing verification in Partner Center
